context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration-4 CRITICAL regression is FIXED and verified. Fix summary: (1) seed_data.py added _badge() helper to avoid Python's str.format() brace-escaping problem — now all six templates keep their {{name}}/{{tracking}}/etc. placeholders intact. (2) seed_data.py added EMAIL_TEMPLATES_VERSION=2 constant. (3) server.py startup replaced count-based idempotency guard with versioned re-seed via db.template_versions collection — bumping the constant now triggers a full wipe+reseed on next startup. This is the correct architectural pattern for template migrations going forward. Backend logs contain 'Re-seeded email templates to version 2' on the startup that ran this migration. No open issues. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py can be used as regression suite by future testing agents (17 tests, ~6s runtime).
rca of the issue: Fixed in this iteration. Root cause was that iteration-3 or earlier had used _wrap(...).format(BADGE) on 4 of 6 seeded templates. Python's str.format() interprets {{...}} as escaped-literal single-brace {...}. Combined with iteration-4's email_service.py refactor that changed the substitution delimiter to double-brace {{...}}, this created a mismatch: the 4 formatted templates ended up with single-brace placeholders in the DB that the new delimiter couldn't match, so users would receive emails containing literal 'Dear {name}, your application {tracking}...'. Fix applied: (1) seed_data.py._badge(label) helper concatenates strings instead of using .format(), preserving double-brace placeholders. (2) EMAIL_TEMPLATES_VERSION=2 constant added, and server.py startup now does a versioned re-seed (delete_many + insert_many) whenever the DB's stored version is below the code's EMAIL_TEMPLATES_VERSION. Verification: iteration_5 test suite exercises (a) DB shape check (all 6 templates have double-brace, no single-brace anywhere), (b) render_template call for all 6 combos with a full context, (c) full E2E status transition flow with email_log inspection — all pass.
